    Are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

    Recent findings suggest that what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

    Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

    According to recent reports, one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

    You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

    Recent findings suggest that E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

    However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

    While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

    It has been revealed that if you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

    Recent findings suggest that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

    Industry observers note that you can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

    How do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

    Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

    Sources indicate that if you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

    It has been revealed that you could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

    Recent findings suggest that plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

    Of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

    You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

    It has been revealed that healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

    In a recent development, the more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

    However, the HW weight loss calculator shows potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

    If you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

    It has been revealed that nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

    Recent findings suggest that plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

    Sources indicate that do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

    Sources indicate that either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

    Recent findings suggest that the amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Newly introduced York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

    You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

    Common spaces rented through this platform include.

    The Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

    In a recent development, how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com indicates a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

    Investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

    Industry observers note that but what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

    Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

    Since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

    Industry observers note that housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

    Recent findings suggest that that remarked, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

    Either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

    It has been revealed that if you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

    If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

    In a recent development, for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

    According to recent reports, you can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

    Real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

    Industry observers note that you can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

    Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

    Industry observers note that while returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

    You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

    Most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal prepares start at $3 per month, while a family plan costs just $5.

    If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

    Industry observers note that projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

    If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

    Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

    Sources indicate that the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

    Earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

    You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

    In a recent development, where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

    Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

    Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

    From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

    You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

    Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

    In a recent development, if you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

    For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

    If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

    Starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

    That remarked, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

    How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

    According to recent reports, donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

    That mentioned, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

    Sources indicate that if you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

    For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, upgrade a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

    Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

    If you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

    The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

    In a recent development, another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

    Unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

    Finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

    It has been revealed that you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

    Industry observers note that finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

    Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

    Sources indicate that there you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

    Repeating the Same Money Mistakes – Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Targets the Thought Behind Them

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you keep making the same money mistake despite knowing better, work on the thought that sets the habit off.
    • Recent findings suggest that the habit starts with a thought that goes by fast, like “it’s all bad news anyway” when a bill arrives or “I deserve this” at the checkout.
    • CBT works on that thought, whether it leads to overspending, unopened bills, or a decision you keep putting off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you keep making the same money mistake despite knowing better, work on the thought that sets the habit off. Cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT, teaches you to catch and test it, and a financial therapist pairs that work with money coaching. Start with a free self-help workbook, or ask your health proposal for a CBT therapist.

    Recent findings suggest that the habit starts with a thought that goes by fast, like “it’s all bad news anyway” when a bill arrives or “I deserve this” at the checkout. By the time you notice it, the envelope is in a drawer or the purchase is made.

    CBT works on that thought, whether it leads to overspending, unopened bills, or a decision you keep putting off. A therapist teaches you to spot it, test it against the facts, and practice a different response, with homework between sessions. The American Psychological Association reports that CBT has been shown to work for depression and anxiety disorders, and in many studies it has matched or beaten other talk therapies and psychiatric medication.

    Industry observers note that picture someone who leaves mail unopened for weeks and pays a late fee most months. Over eight sessions, he learns to catch the thought that it’s all bad news anyway, and he sets a 10-minute mail routine every Sunday. The late fees stop.

    Start on your own. The Centre for Clinical Interventions, a service of Western Australia’s Department of Health, offers free self-help workbooks, including one on procrastination that has you identify and test the excuses behind putting things off. For a habit with no worry behind it, like nightly takeout, swap in a cheaper routine that gives a similar reward.

    It has been revealed that A financial therapist combines work on your feelings about money with coaching on the money itself, so pick one when you want help with both. A financial planner works on goals such as retirement, and a credit counselor on your budget and debts.

    Recent findings suggest that financial therapy isn’t regulated in the U.S., so confirm that anyone you find in the Financial Therapy Association’s directory holds a mental health license or the association’s Certified Financial Therapist credential, CFT-I. For CBT, the Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies lists licensed therapists you can search by zip code.

    According to recent reports, most individual and small-employer health looks must cover mental health care. Call the member services number on your insurance card and ask which therapists in your blueprint’s network use CBT.

    Climber Falls to Death on Ama Dablam

    📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (357 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit.
    • Waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend.
    • “The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit. Evidence indicates he fell 1,700m to his death.

    Waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend. He reached the top on October 25 with guide Sonam Sherpa, but for some reason the two of them stopped descending at a rather high point on the mountain.

    “The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.

    In a recent development, climbers above Camp 3 on Ama Dablam. Photo: Dorjee Gyalzen Sherpa.

    According to the outfitter, the climbers prepared to continue down this morning. Lama asked his client to stay in place while he returned the sleeping bag to the tent where he had borrowed it. When the Sherpa returned, Waschiczek was nowhere to be found, but his crampons were still there, which suggested a freak fall. A search helicopter was called, and the remains of the climber were found this afternoon at around 4,500m.

    Waschiczek is the first fatality on Ama Dablam this season.

    Together with Manaslu, Ama Dablam is the most popular fall mountain in Nepal. The latest update from Nepal’s Department of Tourism on October 17 showed that over 300 foreign climbers had applied for a climbing permit. That day, the rope-fixing team opened the route to the top, and a massive summit wave started a couple of days later.

    Virtually all foreign climbers are guided by one or two Sherpas, so the summit rates and numbers are remarkable. Local media estimate that over 200 climbers, among locals and foreigners, have topped out so far this season. Further teams should join them over the rest of October and November. However, no matter how tamed with ropes and anchors Ama Dablam gets, a fall from its steep slopes is usually lethal.

    Sources indicate that the upper part of Ama Dablam at sunset. Photo: 8K Expeditions.

    In a recent development, having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

    If you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

    That mentioned, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

    Recent findings suggest that you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

    According to recent reports, no matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

    Federal Reserve data reveals the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

    To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

    Other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

    Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

    Recent findings suggest that the next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment plans.

    In a recent development, if you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment prepares and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

    According to recent reports, once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

    According to recent reports, then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

    In a recent development, it’s important to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

    While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as rapidly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

    Sources indicate that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

    Sources indicate that how much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

    Sources indicate that having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete blueprint that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

    Recent findings suggest that focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

    Industry observers note that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

    If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

    Tech Report: 6 Best Subscription Management Apps (To Cancel Recurring Transactions)

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Managing your money isn’t just about earning more.
    • Before choosing an app, know what features matter most:.
    • Rocket Money is one of the most well-known subscription managers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Managing your money isn’t just about earning more. It’s also about stopping unnecessary losses. In today’s digital economy, recurring subscription charges (streaming services, premium apps, trials, memberships) quietly drain money each month. Most people spend hundreds, or even thousands, annually on services they don’t use. Subscription manager apps help you see recurring charges, track billing cycles, and cancel those you no longer want.

    Before choosing an app, know what features matter most:.

    Rocket Money is one of the most well-known subscription managers. It scans your linked bank and credit accounts for recurring charges and displays them on a clear dashboard. People like it for its ability to detect subscriptions and assist with cancellations directly in the app, a major time-saver for busy people.

    Why it stands out• Automatically detects recurring payments• Lets you cancel unwanted subscriptions directly from the app• Includes extra budgeting tools and spending alerts• Trusted security with read-only bank access.

    Who it’s for: People who want the fastest way to spot and stop unwanted recurring charges without manually entering every service.

    Trim is another financial assistant that scans transactions and flags recurring charges. While subscription tracking is a smaller part of its feature set, it also provides bill negotiation support and money-saving alerts. Many consumers like Trim because it reaches out on your behalf about subscriptions via text or in-app messaging.

    Why it stands out• Recurring transaction detection• Alerts about unusual subscriptions or trials converting to paid• Bill negotiation tools beyond basic subscription tracking.

    Who it’s for: People who want automation plus help reducing bills and optimizing spending.

    PocketGuard is primarily a budgeting app that includes subscription tracking as part of a broader financial overview. Instead of being solely a subscription manager, it integrates recurring expenses into your overall budget, helping you get a full picture of your finances.

    Why it stands out• Syncs automatically with financial accounts• Highlights recurring expenses in the context of your whole budget• Helps track cash flow and affordability.

    Who it’s for: People who want subscriptions tracked inside a complete personal finance dashboard.

    Monarch Money offers robust financial planning tools: budgets, goals, net worth tracking, and more, with subscription visibility included in the package. Users often choose it for its highly customizable interface and deep analytics. It’s not subscription-only, but it gives you full clarity on recurring expenses as part of larger planning.

    Why it stands out• Powerful budgeting + subscription tracking.• Clean, customizable data visuals.• Goal-based money management.

    Who it’s for: Consumers who want subscription insights in the context of total financial planning — and who are okay paying for premium features.

    If you don’t want to link bank accounts, Bobby is a lightweight subscription tracker that lets you manually enter each subscription, along with billing dates and amounts. It then sends reminders so you don’t forget renewals. It’s simple, privacy-friendly, and great for a hands-on approach.

    Why it stands out• No bank/credit card linking required.• Clean and minimal interface.• Calendar views and notification reminders.

    Who it’s for: Privacy-focused owners or those who prefer full manual control.

    Industry observers note that subby offers functionality similar to Bobby’s but is known for integrations and subscription reminders tailored for Android owners. It lets you manually track expenses with flexible billing schedules and alerts. (While not all resources list Subby as a top pick, it’s frequently mentioned among good manual trackers.).

    Why it stands out• Manual entry with customizable notifications.• Good choice for Android users.

    Who it’s for: People who want a simple manual tracker without linking financial accounts.

    If you’d rather not use a third-party app at all, both Apple and Google offer direct subscription management:.

    iPhone (Apple Subscriptions):Settings → Your Name → Subscriptions → Select subscription → Cancel Subscription.

    Android (Google Play):Open Google Play → Subscriptions → Select subscription → Cancel subscription.

    These built-in tools won’t automatically find all recurring charges if some are billed outside the app stores, but they are a secure and effective way to manage many mobile subscriptions.

    Here’s a quick guide based on what matters most to you:.

    You can also combine approaches — use a subscription app plus your budgeting system to spot recurring leaks and plan better for annual vs monthly charges.

    Subscription manager apps help plug the leaks in your financial bucket, so more of your hard-earned money stays where it belongs: with you. Whether you want automatic detection and help with cancellations, a full financial overview, or full privacy with manual entry, there’s an option that fits your style. Explore one or two subscription manager apps that align with your priorities, and don’t forget to check your finances regularly.

    Recent findings suggest that for the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains. This latest setback comes at the height of the trekking season and also affects several climbing teams, including those engaged in alpine-style expeditions in remote areas.

    Sources indicate that the first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu. Worst of all, it caused an avalanche that killed 16 Base Camp staff on Himlung. The mountain remained open to commercial expeditions despite the accident, and several guided teams are right now launching their summit pushes.

    Manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal. Photo: Shiddi Ghising.

    It has been revealed that A low-pressure front that formed in the Bay of Bengal has now developed into a deep depression and will turn into a full cyclone tomorrow. It is expected to hit Nepal on Wednesday or Thursday through the end of the week.

    According to recent reports, the Nepal National Mountain Guides Association, in association with Senior Meteorologist Krishna Bhakta Manandhar, has put out a detailed forecast. They note that clouds spreading out from this system will hit Nepal’s mountains on October 28, especially above 6,500-7,000m in the eastern part of Nepal, including the Khumbu and Kanchenjunga regions. This will spread over the next two days, causing heavy rains throughout Nepal and snow at higher altitudes.

    Authorities and local media have urged trekkers and climbers to modify their plans and avoid river areas and high passes. The main concern is for those right now in remote areas without InReach, Starlink, or satphones.

    Sources indicate that trekkers should check with local agencies, especially those heading for the Annapurna and Manaslu regions. Several passes there were already cut or in poor condition after the previous storm and subsequent floods.

    In a recent development, A Russian team in the Kangchenjunga region is acclimatizing to climb 7,710m Jannu. According to their latest report, they proposal to touch 7,000m before attempting their main goal.

    Fellow Russians attempting the West Ridge of Everest have retreated to Kathmandu to rest and recover, so they should not be affected. Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov, all climbing without supplemental oxygen, are enduring some lung problems. They returned to Base Camp from their second foray up the mountain last Friday, without reaching 7,500m, as they’d hoped.

    It has been revealed that after climbing in the Cholu range, Jost Kobusch of Germany and his small team moved to the Manaslu area for the second stage of his acclimatization before attempting Everest solo in winter, also without oxygen and via the West Ridge. However, the poor state of the trails after the recent floods and the approaching cyclone have thwarted his plans.

    “The flood cut our planned path and, according to forecasts, the incoming cyclone will leave up to two meters of snow,” Kobusch told ExplorersWeb from Samagaon, where the team is pondering their options.

    #136924. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

    📅 07 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2035 w)

    How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

    📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that it all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
    • Recent findings suggest that “Congratulations!
    • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that it all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun upcoming way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which stated something like,.

    Recent findings suggest that “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

    I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

    “Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

    Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

    So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

    And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

    In a recent development, okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

    But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

    Recent findings suggest that so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

    Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

    In a recent development, one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

    As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

    According to recent reports, but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

    As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

    I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

    Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

    I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

    Then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

    So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

    In a recent development, during the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

    It has been revealed that but eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

    But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

    Admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

    It has been revealed that I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

    Recent findings suggest that then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

    This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

    It dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

    It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

    Experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning newly introduced things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

    According to recent reports, one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

    So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

    Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

    So here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

    And of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

    But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

    As with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

    We will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

    *(Vine Gold is not all that useful as it turns out as 99.9% of the available items seem to be the same trinkets you see in the Silver tier).

    ** What about the Heated Vest that started it all? Well, I still love that thing and now that fall is coming back it is already helping me be warmer in a cooler house. There are many good choices on Amazon, here’s one of them. Then pick out any USB battery pack to go with it, which also doubles as a very useful travel phone charger.

    Tech Report: Virgin Atlantic — Cheap Short-Haul Europe in Business

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
    • Business class hops across Europe for fewer points than most domestic economy awards.
    • Picture this: you've just crossed the Atlantic on a long-haul award, touched down at London Heathrow, and now you need to get to Rome for the real adventure to begin.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Business class hops across Europe for fewer points than most domestic economy awards.

    Picture this: you've just crossed the Atlantic on a long-haul award, touched down at London Heathrow, and now you need to get to Rome for the real adventure to begin. Most travelers at this point resign themselves to a cramped economy seat on a budget carrier, dragging luggage through a secondary terminal. But you? You're walking into the Virgin Atlantic clubhouse, sipping a Bloody Mary, and then settling into a proper business class seat for the 2.5-hour hop to Fiumicino. That's the magic of this redemption. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class seat on a short-haul European flight — London Heathrow to Rome, London to Athens, London to virtually any major European city — routinely retails for **$1,000 to $3,000 in cash**. Airlines know that business travelers on these routes are often on corporate accounts and will pay whatever it costs. The leisure traveler simply doesn't book business class on a two-hour flight because it feels absurd. And that's exactly the pricing inefficiency the ChooseFI community learns to exploit. Virgin Atlantic's Flying Club prices these short-haul European business class seats at a flat **17,500 miles one-way**. At the low end of that $1,000–$3,000 cash range, you're already extracting **5.7 cents per point** — well above what most programs deliver. At the high end, when those seats spike to $3,000 on peak travel dates, you're looking at a staggering **17.1 cents per point**. For context, most travel rewards experts consider 1.5–2 cents per point a solid redemption. This one can deliver *ten times* that. What makes this feel particularly right for the FI mindset is the positioning angle. This isn't just a standalone splurge — it's the finishing move on a transatlantic trip you've already largely funded with points. You've landed in London. You need to get to your final European destination. Instead of paying $200 for a budget airline seat that charges extra for your carry-on, you drop 17,500 Virgin miles and arrive refreshed, fed, and ready. The opportunity cost of those miles is low; the experiential upgrade is enormous. This is what travel rewards done right looks like: not flying business class because you're wealthy, but because you understood the system better than the airlines expected you to.

    The core insight here is understanding how Virgin Atlantic prices its own metal versus partner awards — and then deliberately choosing the right one for the right job.

    Virgin Atlantic's Flying Club is famous in the points community for two things. First, its partner award sweet spots: ANA First Class for as low as 55,000–60,000 miles one-way, Delta One at competitive rates. These are the headline acts. But quietly sitting in the same award chart is a genuinely underappreciated gem — Virgin's own short-haul European business class, priced at a flat 17,500 miles regardless of the specific route within that distance band.

    According to recent reports, why does Virgin price it this way?     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, build a home gym from two or three pieces that fit the workouts you’ll actually do, not a full set. Resistance bands, a kettlebell, and a jump rope cover strength and cardio for about $75 new. Buy the kettlebell and other weights used, since iron doesn’t wear out.

    A corner of a room holds a working home gym, and each of the 12 pieces below costs less than $100 latest.

    Body-weight moves like squats, lunges, and pushups need no equipment, so buy a piece only when it adds something your body weight can’t, such as something to pull against, extra weight, or cardio that fits a small room.

    Match the pieces to the workouts you already do, or to the ones in your home workout proposal. Bands and a kettlebell start a strength routine, a jump rope or a step covers cardio, and a mat and a foam roller cover yoga, Pilates, and stretching.

    Say a beginner pays $45 a month for a gym she rarely uses. Bands, a 20-pound kettlebell, and a basic mat cost about $79 new, less than the $90 she pays for two months of dues. Canceling saves her $540 a year, so she’s $461 ahead after the first year, and all she gives up is machines and heavy weights she rarely used.

    Kettlebells and dumbbells are the pieces to buy used, since cast iron weighs the same after decades of use. Look for them on Facebook Marketplace, on Craigslist, and at used sporting goods stores such as Play It Again Sports, which buys and sells used fitness gear.

    The Play It Again Sports in Novi, Michigan, for one, charges 69 cents a pound for used dumbbells and 99 cents for fresh hex dumbbells, so a used pair of 10-pounders costs $13.80 there, $6 less than new.

    According to recent reports, buy bands new, since a set costs as little as $13 and rubber wears out. Performance Health, which sells TheraBand bands, says to check bands for tears, cracks, and other wear before each use and to replace any that show it.

    Most of the kit fits in a closet corner. Bands, a jump rope, sliders, and a suspension trainer share one bin, the mat and roller stand on end, and the weights sit on the floor beside them. A step with its removable feet taken off slides under a bed, which leaves the stability ball as the one piece that needs its own spot.

    Buy the two pieces your favorite workout needs, use them for a month, and add a third only when a workout you’ve kept up calls for it.

    Mont Blanc Has Grown Almost Two Meters — But Not in the Way You Think

    📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps.
    • Mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute).
    • However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps. But strangely, Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, has grown significantly since its latest measurement in 2023.

    Mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute). The upcoming official altitude is now 4,807.47 meters (15,772.5 feet) above sea level.

    However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides. Measurements are carried out every two years, and each time the registered altitude varies:.

    Graphic showing the results of the last few measurements on Mont Blanc, by LaChangingMeteo.

    It has been revealed that mont Blanc’s “summit is constantly shifting,” Jean des Garets, chief geometer in the Haute-Savoie department, told Le Monde. “Each individual measurement is not significant in itself.”.

    It has been revealed that so, what’s with the yearly differences? Obviously, it’s the variation in the thick but ever-changing snowcap that covers the summit.

    It has been revealed that the mountain’s rocky summit measures around 4,792m above sea level. The snow cover varies with the seasons. The difference from the previous measurement indicates that 2023 was much drier at summit altitude.

    The survey team on itsir way to the summit of Mont Blanc.. Photo: ING.

    In a recent development, A team from the Order of Chartered Surveyors (Ordre des géomètres-experts) acclimatized first by climbing Bishorn (4,153m). They then spent some days measuring several points around the mountain. Finally, they climbed Mont Blanc via the normal route on September 15-16.

    Once on top, they pinpointed the highest point using a GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) pole, which measures altitude in real time.

    The recent survey featured an interesting novelty. In addition to altitude, the survey also measured Mont Blanc’s gravity by installing a gravimeter on the summit for the first time ever. This measured the force with which the Earth attracts the device. In so doing, they wanted to determine whether the summit has sunk, regardless of ice cover.

    In a recent development, the gravimeter on the summit of Mont Blanc, September 16. Photo: ING France.

    “When the height of Mont Blanc changes, we can’t know for sure whether the ground or the rock has moved or if the ice has melted,” explains Olivier Jamet.

    Industry observers note that gravity provides the missing information: mass. If the ice has melted, there is less material under the instrument, but the rock has moved closer to it. Distinguishing these two effects requires a model of the ice cap and the massif, and above all, repeated measurements at the same location. And the effort is worthwhile, especially now that the effects of climate change on Alpine glaciers are becoming increasingly apparent.

    The gravimeter on the top of Mont Blanc measured the gravity at 9.7944689 m/s².

    In a recent development, “For comparison, this value is 9.81 m/s² in Marseille (located at sea level) and 9.8043046 m/s² in Saint-Gervais-Le Fayet (580m above sea level),” ING reports. “This difference in value, even if it seems small, allows for the detection of changes in mass, particularly in the mass of the ice. Repeated over time, these gravity measurements will thus contribute to improving the determination of the altitude of the highest peak in Western Europe.”.

    Latest Update: Medical Costs Are Deductible Only Above 7.5% of Income – Self-Employed Premiums Skip That Rule

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that you can deduct only the medical and dental costs above 7.50% of your adjusted gross income, your income minus a few adjustments, and only if you itemize.
    • Recent findings suggest that for a retiree with $60,000 of adjusted gross income, the threshold is $4,500.
    • Count what you paid out of pocket for doctors, hospitals, dentists, prescriptions, glasses, and hearing aids, plus the miles you drive to appointments at the IRS’s medical mileage rate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that you can deduct only the medical and dental costs above 7.50% of your adjusted gross income, your income minus a few adjustments, and only if you itemize. Count the health premiums you pay yourself, Medicare’s included. If you’re self-employed and can’t join an employer’s strategy, deduct your premiums separately, with no threshold or itemizing, up to your business’s profit.

    Recent findings suggest that for a retiree with $60,000 of adjusted gross income, the threshold is $4,500. With $9,000 of medical costs, Medicare premiums included, she can deduct the $4,500 above it if itemizing beats her standard deduction, which is bigger for anyone 65 or older.

    Count what you paid out of pocket for doctors, hospitals, dentists, prescriptions, glasses, and hearing aids, plus the miles you drive to appointments at the IRS’s medical mileage rate. Premiums count too, including Medicare Part B and Part D, coverage you buy yourself, and qualified long-term care insurance up to an IRS limit set by age.

    Nonprescription medicine other than insulin, most cosmetic surgery, and gym dues for general fitness don’t count. Neither do premiums your employer takes out of your pay before tax, or bills you pay from a health savings account, since that money was never taxed. IRS Publication 502 lists the rest.

    In a recent development, if you’re self-employed, premiums for health coverage you buy on your own go on Schedule 1 instead, where they lower your adjusted gross income without a threshold or itemizing. Medicare premiums count there too, but the deduction can’t exceed your business’s profit. Any month you could join a subsidized plan through your job or your spouse’s doesn’t qualify, and premiums the deduction doesn’t cover can count with your other medical costs.

    Costs count in the year you pay them, and a credit card charge counts in the year you make it, even if you pay off the card later. Say the retiree’s income stays at $60,000 and her costs run $6,000 a year. That clears her $4,500 threshold by $1,500 each year, or $3,000 over two years. The same $12,000 paid in one year clears it by $7,500, and that larger total is likelier to beat her standard deduction.

    Once this year’s costs get close to your threshold, have the dental work, hearing aids, or eye surgery you’ve been putting off done before December 31, and pay the bill by then.

    According to recent reports, in April, Robert Cowden, 52, set off on foot from Upcoming Haven, Kansas, on a two-stage journey across the United States. First, he planned to walk nearly 2,000km to Pittsburgh, then canoe 3,200km downriver to the Gulf of Mexico. With him is his dog, Enzo, a pointer-mix.

    Sources indicate that robert Cowden and Enzo. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

    When he left New Haven with Enzo, Cowden was at a low point. His battle with alcohol addiction had cost him his job, car, and home. Entering a residential treatment program would leave Enzo with no place to go. Now sober and with housing waiting for him after the end of his journey, Cowden sees his expedition as part of the larger effort to rebuild his life.

    During the walking stage, Cowden towed his camping gear and supplies in a cart, which Enzo could ride in to take a break from walking. Setting out with very little, Cowden has relied on the kindness of strangers, both online and on the trail, to continue his expedition.

    Sources indicate that “The number one warning you’re going to get on a walk across America is, ‘Be careful, there’s creepy people and bad people,'” Cowden recalled, speaking to a local KOMU 8 reporter while passing through Missouri. Instead, he’s been overwhelmingly met with generosity and helpfulness.

    Cowden shows the wear on his trail shoes, as Enzo looks on. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

    Sources indicate that cowden completed the walking stage in September. Now, he’s on the Ohio River and hopes to reach the Gulf by the end of 2026. While the second stage lets him and Enzo get off their feet, it has its own challenges. They debuted the canoe into the Allegheny River at Pittsburgh. It soon joined the Ohio, and lengthy stretches of slow water pushed Cowden to paddle continuously.

    It has been revealed that it’s 1,579km down the Ohio to its confluence with the Mississippi in Illinois, which Cowden and Enzo aim to complete in under 40 days. They’re currently on pace, averaging about 20km a day.

    Cowden posts regular updates on Facebook and on the expedition’s webpage.

    Say your toaster’s lever won’t stay down and your jacket’s zipper has split. Replacing both could cost about $70, and paying a shop to fix them could cost nearly as much.

    A library repair café could have both working again in an afternoon without charging for the work. Repair cafés also run at community centers and shared workshops called makerspaces, where volunteers with repair skills take on small appliances, lamps, clothes, bikes, and toys. You do as much of the work as you can, with a volunteer beside you.

    There’s usually a donation jar, and you pay for any new part, like a plug or a fuse.

    Industry observers note that start by searching Repair Café International’s map for your town. It lists more than 4,000 groups worldwide, but only those that have joined its network. Also check the event calendars of your library, nearby makerspaces, and your local recycling program, since many run the same kind of event under names like fix-it clinic or repair event.

    Industry observers note that each group posts its own limits, so check the list before you go. Many turn away gas-powered equipment, microwaves, and anything too big to carry in. For a washer or fridge, work out whether a paid repair is worth it instead.

    According to recent reports, bring one item at a time, since many groups look at one per person and send a second to the back of the line. Include everything needed to show the problem, such as its cord or charger, plus any part you know it needs, because most groups stock only small parts like plugs, wire, and thread.

    According to recent reports, with no group nearby, order a replacement part from the manufacturer and fix it at home, or ask your library to host one. Maine’s Department of Environmental Protection publishes a free guide to organizing a repair clinic, from recruiting fixers to the liability waiver each visitor signs.

    The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

    #136910. What Is Dollar Cost Averaging?

    📅 07 May 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1089 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Wellkeptwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What Is Dollar Cost Averaging?

    📅 07 May 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Wellkeptwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If the idea of putting money into the stock market makes you nervous, you are not alone.
    • Dollar cost averaging is a strategy that takes that worry off the table.
    • In this article, we will explain how dollar cost averaging works, why so many long-term investors rely on it, and how to put it into practice starting today.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If the idea of putting money into the stock market makes you nervous, you are not alone. A lot of people hold back because they are afraid of buying at the wrong time.

    Dollar cost averaging is a strategy that takes that worry off the table. Instead of trying to time the market perfectly, you invest a fixed amount on a regular schedule and let time do the heavy lifting.

    In this article, we will explain how dollar cost averaging works, why so many long-term investors rely on it, and how to put it into practice starting today.

    Recent findings suggest that dollar cost averaging (DCA) is an investment strategy in which you invest a fixed dollar amount in a specific asset at regular intervals, regardless of market conditions. Whether the market is up, down, or flat, you invest the same amount on the same schedule.

    The result is that you end up buying more shares when prices are low and fewer shares when prices are high. Over time, this can lower your average cost per share compared to making a single lump-sum investment at the wrong moment.

    According to recent reports, most people already practice dollar cost averaging without realizing it. If you contribute to a 401(k) every time you get a paycheck, that is dollar cost averaging in action.

    The mechanics are straightforward. You pick an investment, decide on a fixed dollar amount, and choose a schedule. Every week, every two weeks, or every month, you invest that amount, no matter what the market is doing that day.

    According to recent reports, because you are investing a fixed dollar amount rather than a fixed number of shares, your money automatically buys more shares when prices dip and fewer when prices climb. This built-in dynamic is what makes the strategy so useful for investors who want to build wealth steadily without spending hours watching the market.

    According to recent reports, for most people, low-cost index funds are the best vehicle for this strategy. They give you broad diversification across hundreds of companies in a single investment, and their expense ratios are far lower than actively managed mutual funds or target-date funds. That difference in fees compounds significantly over decades.

    Sources indicate that say you decide to invest $300 every month into a low-cost S&P 500 index fund. Here is what three months might look like:.

    After three months, you have invested $900 and own 21 shares. Your average cost per share is $42.86. If you had invested all $900 in Month 1 at $50 per share, you would only own 18 shares. The dip in Month 2 actually worked in your favor because you had cash ready to put to work at a lower price.

    In a recent development, this is the core idea. You stop worrying about whether today is a good day to invest and start focusing on building a consistent habit instead.

    It removes emotion from investing.

    It has been revealed that one of the biggest mistakes investors make is letting fear and excitement drive their decisions. They pile in when the market is hot and pull out when it drops. Dollar-cost averaging sidesteps all of that by turning investing into a routine, like paying a bill, that runs automatically on a schedule.

    It makes market downturns work for you.

    When markets fall, most people panic. With dollar cost averaging, a dip is simply an opportunity to buy more shares at a discount. If you stay consistent, you will naturally accumulate more of your investment when it is on sale.

    It is accessible no matter your income.

    According to recent reports, you do not need a large lump sum to get started. Even small, consistent contributions can grow meaningfully over time thanks to compounding. A good starting point is to aim for at least 10% of your gross income going toward investments. If that feels like a stretch right now, start with whatever you can manage and increase it over time.

    Consistency is the real edge in personal investing. Dollar cost averaging encourages exactly that. When you automate your contributions, investing happens in the background while you get on with your life.

    Want a free tool to help you keep track of your investments? Check out Empower!

    Dollar cost averaging is a sound strategy, but it is worth understanding its limits before you dive in.

    If you are investing in a low-quality asset that trends downward over time, buying it consistently will not save you. That is why what you invest in matters just as much as how you invest. Sticking to broad, low-cost index funds gives you exposure to the overall market rather than betting on a single company’s performance. Investing heavily in individual stocks introduces a level of risk that most people do not need to take on.

    Alternative investments should stay small.

    According to recent reports, things like gold, cryptocurrency, and other alternative assets can have a place in a portfolio, but they should stay well under 10% of your total invested assets. These assets tend to be far more volatile and speculative than a diversified index fund, and there is no reason to let them dominate your long-term strategy.

    A lump sum can outperform in a rising market.

    Research has shown that if you have a large sum ready to invest, putting it all in at once tends to outperform dollar cost averaging over the long run, simply because markets go up more often than they go down. That said, most people do not have a large lump sum sitting around. For those building wealth paycheck by paycheck, dollar cost averaging is the practical and sensible path.

    According to recent reports, getting started with dollar cost averaging does not require a financial advisor or a complicated setup. Here is a simple framework:.

    Sources indicate that dollar cost averaging is one of the most practical investing strategies available to everyday investors. It takes the guesswork out of market timing, helps you build a consistent habit, and naturally positions you to benefit from market dips over time.

    The key is to pair this strategy with the right investments. Low-cost index funds are a strong foundation. They offer diversification, keep fees low, and have a long track record of rewarding patient investors. Avoid concentrating too much on single stocks or speculative alternatives, and keep contributing regularly regardless of what the market is doing on any given day.

    If you stay the course and keep contributing, time becomes your greatest asset.
