    • Spend your first day at a upcoming job meeting people, not hunting for documents.
    • According to recent reports, expect three forms by day one, and each needs something only you can supply.
    • Industry observers note that the first, Form I-9, has a deadline.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Spend your first day at a upcoming job meeting people, not hunting for documents. The night before, gather your bank details for direct deposit and the documents that prove you can work in the U.S. Once you’re there, ask your manager what success looks like in your first 90 days.

    According to recent reports, expect three forms by day one, and each needs something only you can supply. One proves you can work in the U.S., one sets up direct deposit, and the third, a W-4, sets how much federal income tax comes out of each paycheck.

    Industry observers note that the first, Form I-9, has a deadline. Your employer has three business days from your first day to examine your documents, and it may let you go if they’re missing. A U.S. passport is enough on its own. Otherwise, pair an ID such as a driver’s license with your Social Security card or birth certificate, or pick another pair from the list of acceptable documents. Bring originals that haven’t expired, since photocopies don’t count. For a lost one, bring the receipt showing you’ve applied to replace it.

    Then settle the rest the night before:.

    A upcoming hire who brings her passport and a voided check can finish the paperwork in ten minutes and spend the rest of the morning meeting the team.

    It has been revealed that on day one, arrive a few minutes early, write down names as you meet people, and take notes on how work gets done. Then ask your manager what success looks like in your first 90 days.

    You don’t have to pick your benefits on day one, but the window to enroll is often 30 days from your start. Missing it usually means waiting for open enrollment, which comes once a year at most employers. Find your deadline and put it on your calendar before you leave.

    I recently completed three of the top Christian financial education programs for churches: SeedTime’s True Financial Freedom, Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University, and Crown Financial’s MoneyLife.

    Recent findings suggest that these popular programs all claim to help you get control of your finances from a biblical perspective. However, they go about it in different ways with varying teaching styles and philosophies.

    In this post, I’ll provide an in-depth look at each program – breaking down the unique features, strengths, weaknesses, and what’s actually included when you buy in.

    According to recent reports, my goal is to give you the real deal on these courses so you can determine which one (if any) is the best fit for transforming your financial life in a way that aligns with your faith. Whether you’re deep in debt, building wealth, or simply trying to honor God with your money, this comparison will help guide your journey.

    Let’s dive into the nitty-gritty details of each program:.

    It has been revealed that when it comes to pricing, Financial Peace University from Dave Ramsey sits in the middle. For an individual membership, it’s $69.99. They also offer bulk pricing for churches starting at around $800 for 10 memberships.

    On the higher end, Seedtime’s True Financial Freedom charges $149 for an individual/couple license with regular deals making it available as low as $74. But they have some solid deals for Churches – you can get a bulk student license for as low as $48 per person if you buy multiple licenses. Or there’s an annual church subscription starting as low as $750 per year based on average attendance.

    In a recent development, the most affordable option is Crown Financial’s MoneyLife course at just $29.95 for an individual purchase. I couldn’t find any publicly listed bulk pricing for churches, but being a non-profit, I’d expect them to be the cheapest route for congregations.

    But as you’ll see, there are plenty more differences beyond just the price tags when comparing what’s actually included in each program.

    Sources indicate that true Financial Freedom, created by Bob Lotich and his wife Linda from SeedTime, is a financial literacy video course designed for churches that strikes a beautiful balance between biblical wisdom and practical money management strategies. The program’s goal is to equip Christians with the tools and mindset they need to experience true financial freedom while making an eternal impact for God’s Kingdom.

    Sources indicate that one of the standout features of True Financial Freedom is the engaging and relatable teaching style of Bob and Linda. They share their own financial struggles and triumphs with humor, transparency, and grace, making participants feel like they’re learning from wise, caring friends rather than aloof experts. This approach creates a safe, non-judgmental environment where participants can openly discuss their financial challenges and celebrate their progress.

    According to recent reports, the program offers several unique benefits, such as the “Never 100” rule (their ‘done-is-better-than-perfect’ approach to adjust spending) and the “Straight A” strategy for automating finances. These concepts are not only memorable but also highly actionable in helping participants take control of their money and build lasting wealth.

    Another strength of True Financial Freedom is its emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy. Through interactive workshops, participants are guided in developing a custom blueprint that fits their unique situation, goals, and values. This approach recognizes that there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to personal finance and empowers participants to take ownership of their financial journey.

    True Financial Freedom is perfect for Christians who want to learn how to thrive financially while staying grounded in the Bible. The program teaches participants how to avoid the extremes of being “so heavenly-minded they’re no earthly good” or becoming so focused on building worldly wealth that they lose sight of what truly matters.

    With its grace-filled approach and practical tools, True Financial Freedom helps Christians find the balance needed to change their financial life and make a lasting difference in the world in the process.

    According to recent reports, financial Peace University, created by Dave Ramsey and his team at Ramsey Solutions, is a highly popular financial education program that has helped countless individuals and families get out of debt and build wealth. The program’s primary goal is to guide participants through a proven, step-by-step approach to taking control of their money and achieving financial peace.

    In a recent development, dave Ramsey, the face of Financial Peace University, is known for his high-energy, tough love teaching style. He delivers hard-hitting truths about money with a sense of urgency and conviction that inspires participants to take action. However, some may find his approach a bit intense or even abrasive at times, likening it to going through bootcamp. While this style resonates with some, it may not be everyone’s preferred learning environment.

    The cornerstone of Financial Peace University is the “Baby Steps” system, a clear, prescriptive plan for getting out of debt and building wealth. The program heavily emphasizes the debt snowball method, which involves paying off debts from smallest to largest, regardless of interest rates. This approach has proven highly effective in keeping participants motivated and helping them experience quick wins on their debt-free journey.

    It has been revealed that while Financial Peace University does incorporate some biblical principles, its overall approach is more secular in nature. The program focuses primarily on the practical nuts and bolts of money management, with less emphasis on exploring the deeper spiritual implications of financial stewardship.

    In a recent development, financial Peace University is best suited for individuals and families who are drowning in debt and need a clear, actionable plan to get back on track. The program’s structured approach and intense motivation can be a lifeline for those feeling overwhelmed by their financial situation. However, those seeking a more personalized, grace-filled approach that deeply integrates biblical wisdom may find other programs more appealing.

    Industry observers note that moneyLife, offered by Crown Financial, is a financial education program that takes a deeply biblical approach to money management. The program’s primary goal is to guide Christians in understanding and applying God’s financial principles to their lives, emphasizing the importance of seeing God as the ultimate provider and owner of all resources.

    It has been revealed that one of MoneyLife’s distinguishing features is its strong focus on biblical teachings and spiritual practices related to money. The program dives deep into exploring how our financial decisions can reflect our faith and values, encouraging participants to align their money management with biblical principles. This emphasis on the spiritual aspects of finance sets MoneyLife apart from other programs that may focus more heavily on practical strategies.

    The teaching style in MoneyLife tends to be more academic and classroom-like compared to other programs. Participants can expect a significant amount of reading materials and written assessments throughout the course. While this approach may appeal to those who prefer a studious learning environment, it may not be as engaging for individuals who thrive on interactive, video-based content.

    MoneyLife offers some unique elements, such as personality assessments that help participants understand how their natural tendencies impact their financial decisions. The program also includes exercises like the transfer of ownership, which guides participants in acknowledging God’s ultimate ownership of their resources. These introspective activities can be powerful tools for reshaping participants’ mindsets and habits around money.

    However, one potential drawback of MoneyLife is that its emphasis on biblical principles and spiritual practices may come at the expense of providing highly actionable, practical financial strategies.

    MoneyLife is ideal for Christians who are seeking a deeply biblical understanding of money management and are willing to engage in a more studious, reflective learning process. The program is well-suited for those who want to explore the spiritual foundations of financial stewardship and align their money habits with their faith. However, those primarily looking for a simple and easy financial strategy or a more interactive learning experience may find other programs that better fit their needs.

    Having gone through all 3 programs, here is my personal experience and recommendations:.

    In a recent development, I can honestly say that True Financial Freedom was a life-changing experience. Bob and Linda’s warm, relatable teaching style made me feel like I was learning from trusted friends who truly cared about my success. The program’s emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy was a game-changer for me, as it helped me develop a plan that fit my unique situation and goals.

    It has been revealed that personally, True Financial Freedom struck that balance better than any of the other programs on the list and gave me the strategy to move forward. My savings, giving, and earning have all increased in significant ways since taking the program.

    According to recent reports, for those who are drowning in debt and need a clear, structured initiative to get out, I highly recommend Financial Peace University. Dave Ramsey’s no-nonsense approach and the step-by-step “Baby Steps” system can provide the motivation and direction needed to tackle debt head-on. The debt snowball method, in particular, has helped countless people experience quick wins and build momentum on their debt-free journey. Just be prepared for a more intense, boot camp-style learning environment.

    In a recent development, if you’re seeking a program that deeply explores the biblical principles behind money management, Crown’s MoneyLife might be the right fit for you. The program’s emphasis on spiritual practices and aligning your finances with your faith can be incredibly powerful for those who want to grow in their understanding of God’s perspective on wealth. However, be prepared for a more academic, reading-intensive learning experience and less focus on highly practical, actionable strategies.

    Ultimately, the best program for you will depend on your unique financial situation, learning style, and personal goals. If you’re looking for a grace-filled, practical approach that helps you thrive in God’s Kingdom while making an eternal impact, I highly recommend True Financial Freedom. If you need a structured, intensive blueprint to get out of debt fast, Financial Peace University could be your best bet. And if you desire a deep dive into the biblical foundations of money management, MoneyLife is worth considering.

    According to recent reports, regardless of which program you choose, the most crucial thing is to take action and invest in your financial education. By doing so, you’ll be better equipped to handle the resources God has entrusted to you and experience the joy and freedom that comes from aligning your finances with your faith.

He lives in Greensburg, PA with his wife and two children.

    #136870. Upcoming Route Attempt on Lunag Ri Falls Just Short of Summit

    📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (620 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    Upcoming Route Attempt on Lunag Ri Falls Just Short of Summit

    📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding latest route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border.
    • It has been revealed that the pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif.
    • They placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding latest route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border. They turned back short of the summit, which some sources list as 6,907m.

    It has been revealed that the pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif. The line would have ended on the southeast summit. It involved mixed and rock climbing to M6, aid sections of A2–A3, ice up to WI5–WI6 in places, and long stretches of steep snow with limited protection.

    They placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net. The duo turned back short of the summit due to a coming storm and health complications. The complex summit area — multiple closely linked peaks and ridge features — also left some uncertainty about how close they came to the main summit.

    Even without summiting, this was a significant exploration of a major, unclimbed feature on a remote peak.

    Sources indicate that the new line opened by the Parfenov and Semenov. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

    Lunag Ri, the highest peak in the Lunag massif, has long stood as one of Nepal’s highest unclimbed summits. Early attention focused on the broader massif after Joe Puryear and David Gottlieb made the first ascent of the neighboring 6,778m Jobo Rinjang via its South Face in 2009.

    In the same year, a Swiss-led team under Stephane Schaffter attempted lines in the area, including approaches to Lunag I, though their claims about summits on the massif were later met with skepticism in the American Alpine Journal.

    In the autumn of 2010, a French team that included Max Belleville, Mathieu Detrie, Mathieu Maynadier, and Sebastien Ratel climbed the southeast face of Lunag Ri. Their route, Close the Door (1,200 m, IV/5 F5), was completed in a three-day alpine-style push with two bivouacs. They reached a distinct southeast top (6,812m to 6,830m) on the long ridge connecting Lunag I to Jobo Rinjang. By this time, they were exhausted and did not continue the short remaining traverse to the higher main summit. This remains the only major completed route on the Lunag I massif before the first ascent of the true summit.

    From the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

    Industry observers note that attention then shifted to the west ridge and southwest face of the main peak. In November 2015, Conrad Anker and David Lama’s alpine-style attempt reached a high point roughly 300m below the summit before retreating due to the unexpected complexity of the ridge.

    They returned in 2016 to try a similar line. On the first day, at about 5,800m, Anker suffered a heart attack and was evacuated by helicopter. Lama subsequently continued alone on a variation that moved farther right onto an icefield. He established two bivouacs and pushed 50m higher than the previous year’s high point before turning around 250m shy of the summit.

    In late October 2018, Lama returned solo. Over three days (October 23-25), with two bivouacs, he climbed the southwest face and northwest/west ridge (1,500m of vertical gain, terrain to 90°). He moved mostly ropeless, with limited self-belaying on the harder mixed sections. Lama negotiated the previously unclimbed headwall and made the final exposed traverse onto the main summit.

    Sources indicate that this was the first ascent of Lunag Ri’s highest point. He descended largely by rappelling down the line of ascent. Lama was awarded a Piolet d’Or for this solo first ascent of Lunag Ri.

    From the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

    Family or Friend Won’t Repay a Loan? Get a Payment Strategy in Writing First

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (467 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment initiative they can afford, with a set amount and start date.
    • Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.
    • In a recent development, so skip the hints and make one specific request.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment initiative they can afford, with a set amount and start date. Confirm it in a text they answer. Save a demand letter or small claims court for a broken plan, or forgive the rest and say so.

    Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.

    In a recent development, so skip the hints and make one specific request. Call or meet in private. A text is easy to ignore, and with others listening, embarrassment can turn into an argument. Propose an amount and a schedule they can actually meet. A sister owed $2,400 might ask her brother for $100 a month starting next payday, which clears the debt in two years.

    Afterward, text them a short summary of the initiative and ask them to confirm it. Their reply is a written record that they owe the money and agreed to repay it, which matters if the plan falls apart.

    Industry observers note that if payments don’t start, or start and then stop, put the request in writing. Send a short letter or email that states what they owe, the payments they missed, a deadline to pay, and that you’ll file in small claims court if they don’t. Keep a copy. California’s courts require you to ask for the money before you file, and your copy demonstrates the judge you did.

    According to recent reports, once the deadline passes, file in small claims court. It takes claims up to a cap your state sets, from $2,500 in Kentucky to $25,000 in Delaware and Tennessee. Filing is cheap. California’s fee for a $2,400 claim is $50. For the hearing, bring the bank or payment app record of the transfer and every message in which they agreed to repay you.

    It has been revealed that suing a relative or friend can cost you the relationship, win or lose. When the relationship matters more than the money, forgive the rest on purpose and tell them it’s now a gift, which settles the debt for both of you. Then stop lending to that person. For anyone else, lend only money you could afford to give away.

    Breaking: Floating Alone Down the Brahmaputra on a Bamboo Raft

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River.
    • Recent findings suggest that this won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river.
    • Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River. He set off on a homemade on a bamboo raft from the Dhola–Sadiya Bridge on November 1 and aims to finish at Dhubri, 891km later. The route covers the entire Brahmaputra within India and should take 22 to 25 days in all. The river begins in Tibet and continues beyond India into Bangladesh, covering 2,900km in all.

    Recent findings suggest that this won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river. In 2020, he and two friends took a similar bamboo raft down a 400km section of the Brahmaputra. Earlier, in 2015, Bordoloi was one of 11 who tackled another part of the river over 11 days under the auspices of the Assam Mountaineering Association. This expedition, however, will test his endurance, pitting him against river conditions for longer, and with less support, than ever before.

    Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra. This raft took Bordoloi and friends from the world’s largest river island, Umananda, to its smallest, Majuli. Photo: Shekhar Bordoloi/Instagram.

    Bordoloi’s raft was hand-built from bamboo poles carefully lashed together over several days. Such craft are a traditional way of navigating rivers across the region, and are still used by local communities for fishing and transportation.

    According to recent reports, though the river can be temperamental, Bordoloi’s first two days have been relatively calm, taking him down the Lohit, one of the Brahmaputra’s many tributaries and channels. Navigating the complex river system alone will be a challenge. The Brahmaputra is one of the largest river systems in India, the ninth-largest in the world by discharge, and is prone to flooding and powerful currents.

    According to recent reports, but according to Bordoloi, those obscure, winding corridors are at the heart of this project. Many sections of the river remain underexplored, and he believes there is hidden potential for the people in his home region of Assam. If he can map routes for river tourism and model environmentally responsible river navigation through those routes, he hopes to draw attention to this crucial riverine ecosystem and the economic opportunities for the people living along it.

    Industry observers note that the logistical challenges of a long expedition will further complicate progress. On previous expeditions, Bordoloi traveled with minimal supplies or no food at all, relying entirely on foraging and knowledge of the natural landscape. But this adventure will take over twice as long and may put those skills to their limits.

    Bordoloi is documenting his daily progress on Facebook and Instagram.

    #136867. Details, Video of Jugal II First Ascent

    📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (611 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    Details, Video of Jugal II First Ascent

    📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route.
    • Recent findings suggest that the peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023.
    • Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route. Yet, the climbers insist that the best part of the experience was climbing part of the route with Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet. Jugal II was Strategy B for the Italian pair after flooding washed out access to their primary target, Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region.

    Recent findings suggest that the peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023. In the end, it was the skill and smart strategy of Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain that put them on the unclimbed 6,518m summit after an alpine-style push via the east-southeast face.

    Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.

    Sources indicate that the team noted that the greatest technical difficulties came high on the route. “From the upper bivouac, the climb goes on pretty vertical mixed terrain, with sections of poor-quality rock,” Zabalza explained. “It’s sustained M5 with some even harder sections, until 6,450m. Then the rest of the way to the summit follows along a 55˚-60˚snow slope.”.

    A tough, vertical mixed section. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

    Industry observers note that they reached the summit on October 29, at 4:00 pm. The weather was clear but very cold, with some evening humidity.

    “We made three bivouacs on the route, two on the way up and one more on descent, and all of them were rather precarious,” Mikel Zabalza told ExplorersWeb from Kathmandu. “Luckily, we had a tarp to enlarge them.”.

    One of the climbers on the summit of Jugal II. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

    Industry observers note that the Spanish team, all highly experienced alpinists, had been studying the route for months. This was key to their success.

    Industry observers note that the situation was different for Benet and Meroi of Italy. Since they had not planned to do Jugal II, their approach to the route was more improvisational. They had no previous information about what they would find. To make matters worse, the third member of the team, Tine Cuder of Slovenia, had to abandon the expedition due to health problems.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the Spanish team’s bivouacs, with a tiny ledge enlarged by a fabric tarp. Photo: Romano Benet.

    There was no competition between the two teams, who happily joined forces for the summit push. However, the Spaniards’ strategy proved essential on the highly steep ramps covered with unstable snow.

    Industry observers note that nivel Meroi loaded with bivy gear on highly steep mixed ramps on Jugal II. Photo: Romano Benet.

    “We set off on an adventure, having never seen the mountain before and not knowing what kind of ascent awaited us, but we gave it a try,” Romano Benet reported from Kathmandu. “We decided to turn back to avoid a third bivouac. ”.

    Sources indicate that the two teams joined forces and were in good spirits on the route. Photo: Romano Benet.

    Benet explained that they lacked the necessary gear (specifically, a tarp like Zabalza’s group) to pitch bivvies “on this type of face, where it’s impossible to carve out a ledge.”.

    Industry observers note that otherwise, the two groups returned as friends. “Nives and Romano are exceptional people,” Zabalza noted.

    “We are back from the mountain with new experiences and ideas but, most of all, with three new fantastic friends with whom, hopefully, we will share more adventures in the future,” Romano Benet concluded.

    The Spanish team sent us the video below summarizing the climb.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu. Why are conga lines similar to the infamous ones filmed every May on Everest’s Hillary Step, now repeating at the base of the mountain? We asked the local trekking guide who shot the video.

    Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.

    “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained. “This video was shot on November 1, after three days of continuous snow and rain…During that time, all the trekkers were stuck in Dingboche, which is two trekking stages away from Everest Base Camp.”.

    When the weather finally cleared, all those trekkers set off for EBC at the same time, causing heavy traffic on the route from Dingboche to Gorakshep.

    Industry observers note that the recent cyclone is also the reason why the surroundings are so heavily covered in snow. Usually, the entire trail to Everest Base Camp is dry.

    Recent findings suggest that the fresh snow on Nepal’s peaks is having consequences for those planning to summit trekking peaks. Conditions on otherwise straightforward snow slopes have become problematic, as climbers sink into deep, heavy snow.

    According to recent reports, satori Adventures had to retreat after swimming in snow on the flanks of Mera Peak, in the Khumbu. “Four to five feet of fresh snow made it impossible to move forward above high camp,” leader Furba Sherpa reported.

    Ramesh Gurung noted today that he has retreated from an attempt on 6,119m Lobuche East, another popular Khumbu 6000’er. However, Gurung noted he will try again with another group soon.

    Conditions will change only as the snow transforms under the dimming sun and freezes in the approaching winter temperatures.

    In a recent development, on Ama Dablam, Sherpa climbers struggled to reopen the route to Camp 1 on Tuesday but managed to complete it. The route above Camp 1 follows a steep, mixed ridge with less accumulated snow. Several teams are now on their summit rotations and expect to top out in the next few days.

    Tenzing Sherpa of Gokyo Namaste Lodge has shared some useful information for trekkers who plan to cross the huge Ngozumpa Glacier between Gokyo and Dragnag. The recent snowfall makes the usual route less safe, and he recommends following local people along an easier route between Longbanga Tso (1st Lake) and Taujung Tso (2nd Lake). See Tenzing’s sketch of the route:.

    Alternative route between Gokyo Lakes, suggested by Gokyo Tenzing Sherpa.

    Tenzing also noted that the route from Thame to Gokyo is open, as the Gokyo Lodge Association cleared and reopened the trail from the Gokyo side yesterday. However, conditions on the glacier may change quickly.

    The route across Gokyo is one of the most popular side trips in the Khumbu, for those wanting to enrich their Everest Base Camp trek. The area features stunning scenery, with high mountain lakes, glaciers, and a view of the formidable South Face of Cho Oyu.

    #136863. Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

    📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (932 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • While they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife.
    • Industry observers note that as expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts.
    • Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    While they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife. People who live and work every day among animals are the ones who most often face the consequences.

    Industry observers note that as expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts. Here are some recent incidents.

    Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.

    In Indonesia, 24-year-old Selviana Ambu Kaka was attacked by a crocodile while washing clothes in the Bondo Kodi River. Her fiancé and his sister witnessed a large crocodile emerging from the water, biting Ambu Kaka on the leg, and dragging her into the river. They immediately alerted nearby relatives and authorities, and a search commenced.

    The people of Southwest Sumba, the closest town, organized and combed the area with nets. When they found a large crocodile matching witness descriptions, they hauled it onto shore and killed it. The animal measured nearly 4.9 meters long.

    Early on the morning of October 24, Ambu Kaka’s remains were found approximately 30m from the attack site. She is one of many such victims in Indonesia, which sees more saltwater crocodile attacks than any other country.

    Industry observers note that habitat destruction is largely behind the massive number of human-crocodile conflicts. It’s an understandably hard sell, however, for conservation workers to convince locals that preventing attacks means protecting the perpetrators.

    The victim had recently returned from Jakarta to become formally engaged on October 30.

    Photo: Wikimedia Commons/ Rohit Gangwal, CC BY-SA 4.0.

    It has been revealed that A 65-year-old farm laborer, Tulsi Rama Sawar, was killed by a leopard in state of Maharashtra, just north of Mumbai, on November 1. The noise of the attack summoned help from the locals. By the time they arrived, the leopard had fled, but Sawar was deceased. Her case comes less than a month after a leopard killed a 52-year-old woman in the same area.

    Industry observers note that town residents are demanding immediate government action to capture the animal. If their demands for cage traps and cameras are not granted, locals threaten collective protest. The attacks represent a threat to their lives, but also their livelihoods, as farmers are unable to work the fields out of fear of attack.

    Industry observers note that elsewhere, in Uttar Pradesh near the Nepal border, a 45-year-old farmer named Kennu fought off an attacking leopard, sustaining serious injuries. The man was working in a sugarcane field when the predator leaped out from hiding. Kennu fought back, and the animal retreated long enough for him to flee home, where family members brought him to medical care. Forestry officials have urged agricultural workers to avoid working in the fields alone.

    Farm workers are not the only leopard victims, however. Early in the morning of November 4, a 15-year-old girl was dragged from her home in the Shahdol district of central India.

    It has been revealed that saraswati Singh Gond was sleeping in bed beside her sister on their veranda, which did not have a door. A leopard entered during the night, not even waking her sister. Singh Gond’s body was found approximately 300m from the house. The search for the leopard continues.

    Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Shadow Ayush, CC BY-SA 4.0.

    Sources indicate that leopards are only one of the wildlife threats that rural Indians face. A 55-year-old woman was gathering mushrooms in Utterakand in northern India on October 30 when she was attacked and killed by a wild elephant. Devaki Rana was lifted up and thrown to the ground, her son reported.

    Industry observers note that the incident occurred in one of India’s elephant corridors, which allow highly endangered Asian elephant herds to move between their fragmented habitats. The corridors are essential to conservation, but also present a concentrated area where attacks are more common.

    Another fatal encounter took place in the state of Chhattisgarh in east-central India. A man of between 35 and 40 years of age, traveling by motorcycle with his nephew, came upon an elephant standing in the road. It immediately charged them, killing the uncle, while his nephew managed to hide beneath a parked truck. Eventually, the elephant left, and he was able to escape.

    Locals believe that the elephant in question is one known as Kabra Kaan, which they see frequently and which has been connected with earlier incidents. The Forestry Department, however, has not confirmed this.

    Elephant corridors allow them to pass between the remaining forested areas. Photo: Wildlife Trust of India.

    In Japan, brown bear attacks have been rising for several years. As in many places, human settlements are encroaching on brown bear territory. A decrease in farmland has left no boundary between the urban and the forested worlds. The government has responded with controversial bear culls, despite the concerns of conservation workers.

    In a recent development, the latest incident is very different from the increasingly common attack stories. Late on the night of October 30, an express train running on Hokkaido’s Soya Line collided with a large brown bear. The body of the bear was trapped under the train, and the wheels derailed.

    Sources indicate that A brown bear became trapped beneath the wheels of Sarobetsu No 3. Photo: Hokkaido Railway Company.

    None of the crew or 32 passengers were injured in the crash. However, fearing more bears were in the area, officials kept everyone on the train overnight, until they could be safely extracted the following morning. Company officials have confirmed that this is the first bear-collision derailment in their nearly 40-year history.

    #136862. Cash Is King for Small Businesses – Keep Three Months of Fixed Costs in Reserve

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (487 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Cash Is King for Small Businesses – Keep Three Months of Fixed Costs in Reserve

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Keep a cash reserve worth at least three months of your business’s fixed costs, the bills that don’t shrink when sales do.
    • Recent findings suggest that in 2025, the typical small business with a Chase business account had cash to cover less than 18 days of its usual spending if no money came in, the JPMorganChase Institute found.
    • Industry observers note that size the reserve by fixed costs, not total spending.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Keep a cash reserve worth at least three months of your business’s fixed costs, the bills that don’t shrink when sales do. Hold it in a separate business savings account that pays interest, so a slow season or a customer who pays late doesn’t force you into costly borrowing.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2025, the typical small business with a Chase business account had cash to cover less than 18 days of its usual spending if no money came in, the JPMorganChase Institute found. With that little cash, one major customer paying a few weeks late can leave you short for payroll.

    Industry observers note that size the reserve by fixed costs, not total spending. When sales slow, you buy less inventory, but rent, insurance, loan payments, subscriptions, and the pay of the staff you keep come due in full. If your sales are seasonal, hold three months of those bills plus the part of them your slow-season sales don’t cover, since that gap returns every year.

    To build it, pick a share of a typical month’s profit and set up a recurring transfer of that amount into a separate business savings or money market account that pays interest. Kept out of checking, the reserve won’t get spent on everyday bills, and it stays apart from your household emergency fund, which covers your own bills if the business can’t pay you.

    According to recent reports, say a dental practice’s rent, staff pay, equipment loan payment, and insurance come to $45,000 a month. Its three-month reserve is $135,000, built over two years at $5,625 a month. When an insurer holds up the practice’s claim payments for six weeks, the practice covers payroll from the reserve instead of borrowing, then refills it as the payments arrive.

    Spend the reserve only on a real shortfall, such as a late payment, a slow season, or a broken machine you can’t work without, never on an opportunity like a bulk discount. Refill it from the next money that comes in, before you spend on anything that can wait. With a 13-week cash forecast, you can see a shortfall weeks before it hits. A business line of credit, opened while sales are strong, can cover a gap that outlasts the reserve.

    Sources indicate that pull last year’s bank statements, total the fixed costs, and divide by four for your three-month target. Then set up the recurring transfer before this month ends.

    The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

    Young Climbers Bag New Routes, Including First Ascent, in Rolwaling

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An energetic foursome of young French climbers had a busy time recently in Nepal’s Rolwaling Valley, east of the Khumbu.
    • It has been revealed that as soon as the climbers reached Rolwaling, they had to change their primary goal, which was in poor condition.
    • “Before long, the climbing turned vertical, and the ridge became razor-sharp and exposed,” Bazon wrote.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An energetic foursome of young French climbers had a busy time recently in Nepal’s Rolwaling Valley, east of the Khumbu. Eric Bazon, Pierre Girot, Sophie Jacob, and Kilian Moni did two latest routes, including a first ascent of a 5,205m rocky spire and one very difficult line. They then climbed another peak on a “rest” day.

    It has been revealed that as soon as the climbers reached Rolwaling, they had to change their primary goal, which was in poor condition. Their acclimatization was also progressing more slowly than expected. Instead, they focused their attention on a ridge they saw from their base camp every morning. On October 20, Bazon, Jacob, and Girot set off toward the summit, while Moni waited for them at the base.

    “Before long, the climbing turned vertical, and the ridge became razor-sharp and exposed,” Bazon wrote. The climb took three days on the ridge, bivvies included, and led Bazon, Sophie Jacob, and Pierre Girot to the west summit of ChekiGo (6,128m). It took another full day and one more bivouac to reach base camp.

    Sources indicate that cheki Go’s main summit was first climbed in 2005 by Bruce Normand of the UK and Oliver Von Rotz of Switzerland via the west face. A Spanish team led by Mikel Zabalza first reached the west summit via a direct route up the west face in 2017. The team had just returned from bagging the first ascent of Jugal II.

    “It was quite an intense experience for a ‘secondary’ project: one that combined rock climbing on mediocre granite, improvised protection, and steep snow ridges, all while hauling our ropes on our backs,” remarked Bazon.

    The ridge was technical enough to be a good start: 5c on rock and M4 on mixed terrain. In Alpine grades, the team assessed it as TD (very difficult).

    Sources indicate that the ridge on ChekiGo. Photo: Eric Bazon.

    In a recent development, since the weather forecast looked good for another four days, the team decided to continue climbing. They split into two teams: Bazon and Girot headed for a peak previously climbed by elite American alpinists Domen Kastelic and Sam Hennessey in 2014: Chukyima Go (6,259m). Like their predecessors, the French team approached the west face from the Naa Valley in Rolwaling.

    “There was this direct, narrow, and obvious couloir that simply begged to be climbed,” Bazon reported.

    The climbers at an open bivy. Photo: Eric Bazon.

    The next morning, they found the west face in great condition, which allowed them to climb a direct route to the summit along rock cracks, steep ice, and varied mixed terrain.

    According to recent reports, it took them two days (October 27-28), with one cold bivy on the face with their feet in their backpacks, to complete the route’s 23 pitches. Their West Face Direct route is 900m long, and the team assessed it as ED (extremely difficult), with M6 on mixed sections, and an Alpine ice grade of AI5.

    The photo below reveals that the upcoming French route, TchikitaMa Go, runs to the right of the previous line opened by the two Americans.

    Industry observers note that left: the new route opened by the French team, compared, right, to the 2014 line by Domen Kastelic and Sam Hennessey. Photo: Eric Bazon/PlanetMountain.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, Sophie Jacob and Kilian Moni went for an unclimbed peak that also rose right in front of their base camp: 5,205m Janjmu. The pair completed the first ascent on an aesthetic 600m line up the north face. They called the route The Eternal Stars (“Les etoiles eternelles”) after some friends who had recently perished.

    “It felt just like being at home in the Alps, with the added challenge of high altitude,” the climbers reported. “We pushed ourselves to the limit, both physically and mentally, across demanding yet incredibly logical pitches.”.

    It has been revealed that but this was still not enough for the pair. They squeezed in a final climb of Yalung Ri in what they called “a contemplative, active recovery” day. They then finished the trip by paragliding from the summit.

    Sources indicate that kilian Moni flies from the top of Yalung Ri. Photo: Kilian Moni.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Caleb McDaniels, 25, and Henry Penfold, 22, have completed their impressive expedition around Baffin Island.
    • Sources indicate that the pair began and ended in Iqaluit, Nunavut’s capital.
    • The pair’s completed route around Baffin Island.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Caleb McDaniels, 25, and Henry Penfold, 22, have completed their impressive expedition around Baffin Island. The Americans combined skiing, hiking, and packrafting to almost circle the world’s fifth-largest island. McDaniels told ExplorersWeb they did about 20% skiing and the rest was evenly split between backpacking and packrafting.

    Sources indicate that the pair began and ended in Iqaluit, Nunavut’s capital. The final section of their trip was also the longest, a 1,130km stretch with no villages after Igloolik to resupply. They made light work of it, knocking it out in 40 days and bringing their total distance to 3,262km over 145 days, from their late May start to their return to Iqaluit in mid-October. By then, the oncoming Arctic winter gave them few hours of light to work with.

    The pair’s completed route around Baffin Island. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

    Recent findings suggest that with no resupply points, the pair left Igloolik with 82kg of food. They hoped to do it in seven weeks but brought even more food, because they weren’t sure how long that giant giant section would actually take, explained Caleb McDaniels.

    It has been revealed that “With no way to carry that much weight in our packs, we loaded up our packrafts and paddled the first 400 miles [644km]. Then, for the final 300 miles [483km], we heaved on our packs to walk overland,” they explained.

    The paddling portion went quickly, aided by some ingenuity. “Much of the time, we were able to sail using our trekking poles as masts and panels cut out of an old tent for sails. Speeding along at over five mph, we did some incredible downwinding, spray flying from our bows.”.

    Using makeshift sails. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

    In a recent development, postholing through early winter snow back to Iqaluit. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

    “It was more of a postholing session — we slowly picked our way across snow-covered boulder fields and partly frozen marshlands. Constantly breaking through thin ice over the tundra marshes, we walked in our drysuits to keep our legs and feet dry. Each morning required half an hour of chipping ice and melting out our shoes, which invariably froze solid,” they stated.

    McDaniels and Penfold had planned a roughly circular route around the island, but “we weren’t trying to circumnavigate Baffin,” McDaniels told ExplorersWeb. Two previous parties had circumnavigated the island by dogteam, but McDaniels and Penfold’s route was driven by aesthetic considerations rather than to satisfy a catchy trip definition.

    Industry observers note that slogging overland. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

    They chose their route after looking at satellite images and enjoyed both spectacular scenery and some special wildlife sightings, including at least one that was a little too close for comfort.

    “One morning, as I went to fill our water bottles, I stumbled upon a sleeping polar bear hidden behind a low rise. Only a few yards away, it lifted its massive white head and glared at me for a moment before returning to its nap in the sun,” McDaniels wrote. “I carefully retreated behind the rise and yelled over to Henry to get the shotgun and flares out just in case. We quickly packed our boats and got on the water.”.

    In Foxe Basin, they almost collided with a sleeping walrus, and on Nettilling Lake, they met one of the resident seals. “He was immensely curious and not at all afraid. He swam around our boats for half an hour, playing with our stern lines and swimming back and forth between us. At one point, I put my hand into the water, and he brushed it with his nose!”.

    #136859. Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

    📅 25 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3276 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

    Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

    📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.
    • When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.
    • But even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Wow, how about that stock market?

    It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.

    When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.

    But even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry. Because that just means an even bigger crash is coming, right? Especially when this boom-bubble is built on the back of something as frenzied as the present Artificial Intelligence boom… right?

    In a recent development, for those who have been happily tuned out of this drama and just enjoying life: Congratulations! Keep up the great work. But just to give you a quick background for the purposes of this article, here’s the AI story in three points:.

    Investors worry that while AI is definitely a major invention, the mania around it is still too much, too fast, and thus we are due for an even bigger version of the dot com crash we had in the early 2000s. Which happens to be an interesting subject for me, since that was the boom that boosted my own early career and got me on the path to early retirement … before the ensuing crash almost cost me my job and my citizenship application.

    As an aging Internet Financial Guru, I have the privilege of getting lots of questions about this investment cycle, just as I have about past booms and busts. And to address them, I decided to not only write this blog article but also create a little talk about it – which I already gave for the first time at an event called Camp FI Midwest earlier this month. I also hope to polish it up and deliver an improved version at the Bogleheads conference in November.

    Recent findings suggest that so what that means is that today you not only get a blog post, but a few silly presentation slides to go with it for extra entertainment. All with no need for a plane ticket or all that hassle of leaving your house. So let’s get into it!

    According to recent reports, so I recently hit 21 years of retirement. This means I’ve grown pretty comfortable with the idea. But it still threw me for a loop one time when a friend asked me this question:.

    According to recent reports, “How can you be retired, and comfortable in your retirement, and sleep at night, with everything that’s going on in the world? Aren’t you worried?”.

    And I was like, “No, what should I be worried about?”.

    But if you’re a news watcher and a worrier yourself, you can probably think of a few things I should be worried about. Perhaps stuff like this:.

    You’ve got our corrupt and/or dangerous politicians like Trump and Putin menacing the world. Inflation eroding our purchasing power, the AI Bubble, the towering US National Debt, the Iran war and the Ukraine war and all these other wars that are just on the verge of tipping us all into destruction.

    But it turns out these were not the things my friend was asking about.

    Because she actually asked me this question over twenty years ago… In the year 2006. So back then we were worried about entirely different things, right?

    Back then we had corrupt and/or dangerous leaders like Bush, Hussein and of course Bin Laden. There was still a war in the middle east but it was Iraq instead of Iran. We were still worried about the National Debt and Inflation. And we also worried about our overvalued stock market. But back then it was because of the housing bubble instead of the AI bubble. And instead of AI taking our jobs it was going to be outsourcing to India and China.

    Oh and here’s an interesting one: There was a big debate over Peak Oil, and whether the world was doomed because fossil fuel use was always increasing while supply was bound to decrease. And it turns out the opposite happened as you’ll see below.

    So then after all this worry in 2006, what ended up happening?

    Well we did get the Great Financial Crisis, which was caused by a combination of irrational exuberance over increasing house prices combined with a foolish degree of fancy leverage in the financial instruments used to issue mortgages. And it was the biggest crash since the Great Depression.

    But even in that craziest of situations, look how minor it looks in the big picture. A $100,000 investment still ended up ballooning into $852,000 today. And if you look carefully in here you can just see the Covid Crash tucked in there in 2020. Remember that?

    And not only that, the rest of the world got a lot better too:.

    The portion of people living in extreme poverty dropped from 20% in 2005 to only 8% over the next 20 years. Infant mortality – children who die in their first year of life – was cut in half. Clean energy became a thing as solar panels became about 40 times cheaper. So solar generation now makes up the vast majority of all the new generation we add today (the equivalent of 647 nuclear power plants of peak capacity added last year, but with much cheaper and easier solar panels). And sales of pure electric cars have gone from zero up to about a quarter of all the cars sold on Earth last year, on its way to 100%, which is where they already are in Norway.

    So if we circle back to that question my friend asked me 20 years ago: do you think I should have focused my energy on worrying about an uncertain future, or optimism?

    Which of course brings up the question: Is it different this time?

    Recent findings suggest that maybe the US national debt is finally substantial enough to really start messing with us. Maybe the AI bubble is way bigger than the housing bubble and we won’t bounce back from this next stock market crash. Or maybe AI will spin out of control into a super intelligence that takes over the planet and realizes it does not need us any more.

    And the financial media loves to spin a good scary story about all of this. But you know what the fear mongers all seem to be missing?

    It’s the fact that at the core, our prosperity does not come from the financial system or the stock market, which are just some made-up numbers on some computers.

    Really, Prosperity comes from Productivity.

    We first covered this lesson right here on MMM, in the 2014 Classic entitled, “Why we are not really all doomed”. And sure enough, twelve years later the timeless lessons therein remain just as true now as they were back then.

    Sources indicate that and the lesson is really simple: the world of capitalism is always choppy and prone to wild swings. But if you peek beneath the waves, there are real people in there, doing real work and coming up with real inventions.

    Industry observers note that in fact, the very idea of an “economy” or a financial system is just another human invention. If the whole system crashes because we don’t like the numbers we see in there, we can literally make up some fresh numbers and then get back to work. Which is exactly what we did in 2008 and many times before that, and it seems to have worked just fine.

    Meanwhile, we still have every tool we ever invented to boost our productivity. And our standard of living, and our economic growth, and our possibility of retiring early, all come from high productivity.

    But even Productivity and Prosperity aren’t all that crucial.

    Industry observers note that because once we reach a certain standard of living, human happiness kind of tops out in that dimension. In first-world countries, we blew past those minimum requirements several decades ago. And then we start looking for other factors to maximize our overall happiness. All anybody really wants is to lead the happiest, most satisfying life they can manage.

    And when you think of it that way, your wealth is really just part of your life situation, which is part of this little green slice of the happiness pie.

    Sources indicate that genetics is unfortunately the biggest slice – some people are just plain happier than others. But there are also quite a few choices that are within your control.

    According to recent reports, focusing on good close relationships and being kind to people. Practicing Gratitude and Optimism as your lifelong philosophy. And making sure you pack as many healthy (outdoor) activities into your days as you can.

    So, I didn’t invent anything new in this blog post. And most of it is just a repackaging of the same stuff I’ve been writing about since 2011. And yet some regular MMM readers who presumably know all this stuff are STILL afraid. Afraid to retire, afraid of things in their unknown future. Can we fix this?

    I think the biggest problem is Fear Itself.

    Industry observers note that the problem is that as a Human Being, you are basically a Danger Detection Machine. And this pervasive background fear is just a trait we evolved to protect ourselves from danger.

    Recent findings suggest that but there’s a weird thing about our detection machinery. We can adapt and learn to function even in very dangerous environments, but when the danger goes away, we keep looking for stuff to worry about. In other words, there is a problem with fear: for many of us, it never really goes away. It just keeps moving the goalposts.

    While Nature has wisely endowed us with a fear of predators and disease, if you solve those things you’ll just start worrying about whether or not you can get enough food. And supplies, and protecting yourself against scarcity.

    If you succeed, next you’ll be worrying about if you can fit in with your tribe, because if you don’t, you might be exiled.

    Industry observers note that and if you don’t have to worry about that, you’ll go back to worrying about money for different reasons. Thanks to our tendency to use comparisons rather than absolutes (sometimes called “anchoring bias” and the “contrast effect”) when judging our lives, just getting out of poverty isn’t enough. We just move on to wanting more money.

    And then, when some people get enough money to have a comfortable upper-middle-class lifestyle, they take the logical next step of starting a Homeowner’s Association, so they can worry about the unauthorized weeds on their neighbor’s lawn. Or maybe a Political Action Committee in hopes of controlling the color of their future neighbors’ skin.

    And even if all the lawns and gardens are green and perfect and people get really rich, they just move on to worry about tax strategy, leaving a huge inheritance for their children, and avoiding RMDs.

    It has been revealed that required minimum Distributions. This is when, if you get to 75 years old and you have too much money, the government will start making you withdraw some of that money so you can spend it and pay taxes on it. And people actually worry about this. I shit you not.

    Sources indicate that but wait! You can actually fight back against fear. It’s just a bit tricky because it requires some self awareness. But you have the advantage, because you have the ability to think rationally. And your fear is quite clearly irrational.

    Recent findings suggest that and the first step is to understand your own history. Are you afraid of certain things because of your childhood?

    I might have been afraid of running out of money, because in my family there was always a perceived shortage of the stuff, possibly enforced by my Dad’s scarcity mentality. And he was aware that his own fears of scarcity came from childhood as well: he grew up in a truly low income family in the 1940s and 50s, under the care of parents who had lived through the Great Depression of the 1930s.

    Industry observers note that even more significant is that survivors of trauma and abuse will very likely end up with fear issues in adulthood. It’s natural, and unfortunately abuse is way more widespread even in this country than we would like to admit. This makes it harder to eliminate, but it still helps to understand that your past is what is causing these feelings, rather than an objective understanding of the present.

    Sources indicate that identify the Fear: Once you understand yourself, it helps to talk through the nature of your fear in more detail. This is also often taught in therapy. What would happen if it really came true? What would the worst case scenario be? It’s often not all that bad.

    In one post, why you’ll probably never run out of money, I went to great lengths to imagine what it would mean for a wealthy person like yourself to actually let the well run dry, and let’s say you’ll probably never come close.

    Once you identify the fear, you can start taking action. And one of the best and most accurate slogans ever is that action cures fear. It’s because it makes the unfamiliar, familiar. And you get confidence that you can really create change. And then that learning creates Resilience – the ability to adapt to ANY fresh situation, which is a trait also known as Badassity. And with sufficient Badassity, nothing is scary.

    Think about it: if you had the skills and abilities to handle ANY situation, skills in the mental and physical and even the realms of emotion and wisdom, would you really have to worry about anything?

    Sources indicate that the next thing you can do is tune out all the unnecessary crap from your daily mental diet. And for most Americans, this means the daily news.

    The news is not helping you to keep informed, it’s just poisoning your mind with a hand-picked selection of the scariest stories of each day. If you want to learn about something, go find a book on the subject. And if you want to make a difference, the only thing that counts is not the news stories you watch – it’s only the actions that you take – in other words, your Positive Behaviors.

    Sources indicate that as a human being, you are wired to solve problems with both your body and your mind, and you are meant to do it outdoors. So if you spend all your days in a house and a car and in an office using the computer, of course you are going to have some mental health problems. This should not be a surprising thing you need to ask your therapist about, it is an expected result of not living the life that you were literally created to live as a Human being!

    So you need to focus on learning, moving, and solving problems. And you need your food and drink intake to be in alignment with all of this too. Life will get a lot less scary as soon as you are living life in the way you were built to live it.

    Then finally, you can start swapping out the fear-mongers in your life, for other positive, productive, optimistic people. And watch how much the positive mentality rubs off on you. In the FI community, at least the subgroup of people that I like to spend time with, nobody focuses on fear. It’s all just about living the best life we can, and helping other people do so as well.

    So now that we know how to fight back against fear, we can start using a new approach when we go into anything new. And that approach is something I like to call Everything is an Experiment.

    Sources indicate that and this applies whether you are talking about something tiny like a new paint color. But it scales up to bigger things like switching to a new car, or a new house, meeting new friends, looking for new love by going through the sometimes hell of first dates, a new job, or even quitting your last job by taking an early retirement.

    So let’s bring this back around to AI, the thing that everybody seems to be afraid of right now.

    I think of our newly introduced AI era as just being another giant experiment. And because of this, I don’t find it even remotely scary. But I do find it endlessly fascinating.

    First of all, it’s a change. A potentially unknown one, and for some people that’s scary.

    In a recent development, but instead of just leaving it there and then doom-scrolling ominous news articles about it, why not learn why people are so excited about AI? As someone with a lifelong background in technology and economics (and a general lack of political affiliation), I can see a lot more potential upside than downside. And that mainly comes from the fact that I see AI as just a very fancy form of Cognitive Nail Gun.

    Industry observers note that it will boost our efficiency, which means our productivity, which means prosperity. Because it’s really just a super smart brain that we all get to tap into at a fairly negligible cost.

    It has been revealed that unfortunately, it will also displace workers like every other upcoming productivity technology. It’s already doing so in things like entry level office jobs in software and finance. It will eventually replace car and truck drivers, and so on. But in exchange, these services will become cheaper, and new industries will be created because of the new technology. Much like the Internet itself, and then the enormous industries unleashed by smartphones and mobile apps.

    It has been revealed that and one unfortunate side effect of these new inventions is that they tend to concentrate their rewards on the people who own them. If you own a house building company and employ a bunch of carpenters and give nail guns to the best of those carpenters, you can now lay off the other half and still get more done. If you own a company and roll out AI to the workers, you can do the same thing.

    Sources indicate that and if you’re a major public tech giant, your shareholders also benefit, which happens to include most of the people reading this. As you’ve seen when looking at your portfolios over the past two years.

    Artificial Intelligence is just like any other latest thing that pops into your life: it’s an opportunity to make some choices. And it is up to you to decide if this is something to be afraid of, or to use as a trigger for learning, action, and living a more interesting life.

    So that’s my little talk (and surprisingly long blog post) on Fear versus the AI bubble.

    It has been revealed that I hope that if you do feel fearful about this or any other issue in your future life, you’ll take it as a cue to learn more about your own fear and emotions and manage them as the root cause they are, rather than just trying to avoid the symptoms. Because in the wise words of my friends The Donegans:.

    In a recent development, everything you want in life, that you don’t already have,lies on the other side of Fear. Because if you weren’t afraid to go out there and get it, you would already have it.

    #136858. Stepped-Up Basis – Heirs Owe No Tax on Past Gains if You Hold Your Winners

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (448 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Stepped-Up Basis – Heirs Owe No Tax on Past Gains if You Hold Your Winners

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, stocks, funds, and property you leave your heirs get a stepped-up basis, meaning each one’s cost for tax purposes becomes its value on the day you die.
    • Selling an investment that has grown for decades means paying tax on all that growth, and giving it to your children passes the taxable gain to them.
    • Say a father bought shares for $20,000 that are worth $220,000 when he dies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, stocks, funds, and property you leave your heirs get a stepped-up basis, meaning each one’s cost for tax purposes becomes its value on the day you die. The growth during your life then escapes capital gains tax. Hold your biggest winners rather than selling or giving them away, and sell your losers while you’re alive.

    Selling an investment that has grown for decades means paying tax on all that growth, and giving it to your children passes the taxable gain to them.

    Say a father bought shares for $20,000 that are worth $220,000 when he dies. His daughter inherits them with a $220,000 basis, so if she sells them right away for $220,000, she owes no tax. Had he given her the shares a year earlier, she’d have taken on his $20,000 basis with them, and the same sale would leave her a $200,000 taxable gain.

    The step-up covers investments in taxable accounts, such as stocks and funds, plus real estate and other property. It doesn’t cover traditional IRAs and 401(k)s, whose withdrawals your heirs pay income tax on, just as you would. On property a married couple owns jointly, only the half that belonged to the spouse who died steps up, under IRS rules. In a community property state, where most of what spouses acquire while married belongs to both, the couple’s shared property usually steps up in full.

    According to recent reports, so when you need money, spend cash or sell investments with little gain first, and keep your biggest winners. Sell losing investments while you’re alive, since the basis of an investment worth less than you paid drops to its lower value at death, and the loss you could have deducted is gone. With a house, leaving it to your children usually costs them less tax than gifting the house during your life.

    Bills to tax gains at death have come up in Congress, including the Equal Tax Act introduced in March 2026, but none has passed.

    Heirs should get each asset’s date-of-death value in writing, from the brokerage for investments and an appraiser for real estate, and keep it, since any later sale’s taxable gain is measured from it.

    Bank Error on Your Statement? Report It in Writing Within 60 Days

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (494 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Spot a debit card charge, transfer, or direct deposit on your bank statement that looks wrong?
    • Industry observers note that regulation E, the federal rule for electronic transfers, gives you 60 days from the statement to report an error, whether or not you’ve noticed.
    • In a recent development, A phone call counts as reporting the error and starts the bank’s 10 business days to investigate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Spot a debit card charge, transfer, or direct deposit on your bank statement that looks wrong? Call the bank and follow up in writing within 60 days after it sent that statement. Federal rules then usually give it 10 business days to investigate, or longer if it credits your account while it does.

    Industry observers note that regulation E, the federal rule for electronic transfers, gives you 60 days from the statement to report an error, whether or not you’ve noticed. Read each statement the week it arrives, and turn on real-time alerts for large or unusual charges.

    In a recent development, A phone call counts as reporting the error and starts the bank’s 10 business days to investigate. The bank can require you to confirm in writing within 10 business days of your call. It must say so on the call and give you the address. Without that letter, the bank can leave the money out of your account until it decides.

    Paper checks fall outside Regulation E, and you usually have 30 days or less from the statement date to report a check error. Your account agreement sets your bank’s exact deadline. A wrong credit card charge follows a different law, with its own steps to dispute the charge. Report fraud the day you spot it, since what you can lose grows the longer you wait.

    Send the letter the day you call, and keep a copy. Give your name and account number, the transaction’s date and amount, and why it’s wrong. Say a $482 debit card charge shows up twice. You call and write 20 days after the statement, and the bank returns the $482 within a week.

    To take longer than 10 business days, the bank must credit your account for the disputed amount within them, though it can hold back up to $50 for a transfer it believes someone else made. It then has up to 45 days from your call, or 90 for a debit card purchase or a transfer started outside the U.S. For a transfer within 30 days of an account’s first deposit, the 10 business days become 20 and the limit is 90 days. A bank that finds no error must explain why in writing and, on request, send copies of the documents it relied on.

    If the bank finds no error and you disagree, file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and attach your letter and its explanation.
